map.summary: This area is the web front door for an evidence-first enterprise search product: a Next.js page that currently shows a placeholder landing screen with a heading and a note that a search workspace is coming. It is served by a container that runs the development server on port 3000, and it reads no data, stores nothing, and sends nothing. Search, retrieval, and answering are not implemented or connected here yet; a test checks the heading, and code-quality tools check the sources.
unknowns: No calls to any answer service, document storage, or search system appear in the web sources, so how this site would reach those systems is unconfirmed.
The landing page has no input fields, controls, or state, so the intended search workspace behavior is not shown.
The web server configuration declares no forwarding or routing rules, leaving any path from this site to backend services unspecified.
The container starts the development server rather than a production build, so production serving behavior is not demonstrated.
No evidence shows the answer, storage, or search systems calling back toward this website, so any inbound contract is unverified.

diagrams.title: How a visitor gets the landing page
diagrams.description: A visitor opens the site, the page shell supplies styling and page title, and the static landing content appears. Nothing is looked up or saved, and no search runs.

diagrams.title: How the page is checked before release
diagrams.description: Automated checks run the landing content in a simulated browser and verify the heading text, while code-quality tools scan the source. These checks do not exercise any search or backend behavior.

F0001.statement: The frontend container image installs dependencies with npm ci from package.json and package-lock.json, copies the source tree, and starts the Next.js dev server bound to all interfaces via 'npm run dev -- --hostname 0.0.0.0', exposing port 3000.

F0002.statement: The image runs the development server (next dev) rather than a production build/start, so production serving behavior is not shown by these files.

F0003.statement: The package is a private Next.js 16 / React 19 web application, pinned to Node '>=22 <23', with next dev/build/start scripts driving the App Router.

F0004.statement: The user-facing entry point is the App Router root layout (RootLayout in src/app/layout.tsx), which imports the global stylesheet, declares page metadata (title 'Hybrid RAG Search', description 'Evidence-first enterprise search'), and wraps the page children in an html/body shell.

F0005.statement: The index route (Home in src/app/page.tsx) is purely static markup: an eyebrow label 'Hybrid RAG Search', an h1 'Evidence-first answers, built for inspection.', and a note that the search workspace is ready for its first collection. It has no state, props, inputs, event handlers, or async data loading.

F0006.statement: No fetch call, API route, database access, environment-variable read, rewrite, or redirect appears in the supplied frontend sources, so any runtime linkage from this frontend to the answers, foundation, or retrieval subsystems is untraced.

F0007.statement: Next.js config enables reactStrictMode and disables agentRules (a Next option), with no rewrites, redirects, headers, or proxying declared, leaving client-to-backend routing unspecified.

F0008.statement: A Vitest test renders the Home component in jsdom and asserts a level-1 heading with the text 'Evidence-first answers, built for inspection.', providing the only observed automated check of the page's rendered output.

F0009.statement: The test toolchain is configured with the Vite React plugin and jsdom environment, so component tests run in a simulated browser DOM rather than a real one.

F0010.statement: eslint.config.mjs applies Next.js core-web-vitals and TypeScript rule sets and ignores build/coverage outputs; this gates source quality but is a development-time concern, not runtime behavior.

F0011.statement: The lint, format, typecheck, and test scripts (eslint --max-warnings=0, prettier, tsc --noEmit, vitest run) define static quality gates over the sources without executing application logic.

F0012.statement: tsconfig.json establishes strict TypeScript compilation for ES2022 with no emission, React JSX transform, bundler module resolution, and a '@/…' path alias mapping to './src/*'.

F0013.statement: next-env.d.ts is a generated, non-editable type reference file pulling in Next.js and image type declarations plus generated route and root-param types; it carries no runtime behavior.

F0014.statement: The observed end-to-end flow is: a viewer requests the index route, the root layout supplies the HTML shell, stylesheet, and metadata, and the static Home component renders the heading and workspace placeholder; no data is read, stored, or sent.

F0015.statement: The product purpose indicated by naming and copy is an evidence-first enterprise 'hybrid RAG' search workspace, but the supplied files only show a placeholder landing page, so search, retrieval, or answering capability in the frontend is not evidenced.
